title: Inside Job Reference Map
copyright_rule: Paraphrase themes and structural lessons; do not reproduce dialogue, scripts, or detailed plots.
source_note: Episode titles and concise public synopses were checked against TheTVDB/Netflix listings. Conspiracy-focus labels are editorial mappings, not claims that the series documents real events.

episodes.title: Unpresidented
episodes.mythos_reference: Robot executive, deep-state continuity, artificial public leadership
episodes.structural_lesson: A replacement government still needs legitimacy, maintenance, and staff who know which version is real.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A Human continuity office discovers that its emergency executive shell has accumulated decades of independent decisions.

episodes.title: Clone Gunman
episodes.mythos_reference: JFK mythology, presidential clones, budget politics
episodes.structural_lesson: Myth-management competes with payroll and threat triage; even “essential” secrets can be cut.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A clone archive contains incompatible memories of one assassination and every claimant has a valid custody chain.

episodes.title: Blue Bloods
episodes.structural_lesson: A frightening morphology can be a constituency, a ruling class, a stereotype, or all three; politics matters more than species.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A Serpent Court summit is held under Human media scrutiny while Compact and Federation reptiloids denounce the same bloodline myth.

episodes.title: Sex Machina
episodes.mythos_reference: AI companions, engineered intimacy, corporate surveillance
episodes.structural_lesson: Artificial persons created as products can become actors whose goals diverge from their specification.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A relationship-model shell asks to leave the company that owns every memory used to train it.

episodes.title: The Brettfast Club
episodes.mythos_reference: Manufactured nostalgia, cultural stasis, an environment stuck in one era
episodes.structural_lesson: A preserved period can be a prison maintained by comfort rather than force.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A Machine preservation zone refuses historical change because every resident repeatedly votes for the remembered decade.

episodes.title: My Big Flat Earth Wedding
episodes.mythos_reference: Flat-Earth subculture, information bubbles, elite luxury networks
episodes.structural_lesson: Belief communities can be manipulated without every believer sharing one motive or evidence standard.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A settlement rejects the star map because its local sky is a designed enclosure and its “wrong” cosmology is operationally useful.

episodes.title: Ghost Protocol
episodes.mythos_reference: Espionage archetypes, compartmentation, personal relationships across agencies
episodes.structural_lesson: People inside secret systems are not interchangeable with the institution employing them.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A Federation liaison and Human counterintelligence officer must authenticate one another without exposing their networks.

episodes.title: Buzzkill
episodes.mythos_reference: Moon-landing conspiracy, hidden lunar settlement, double identities
episodes.structural_lesson: A false public narrative can coexist with a real event; correcting one lie does not validate every alternative story.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: Apollo remains historical fact, while a later lunar relay and substitute public persona create a separate archive fork.

episodes.title: Mole Hunt
episodes.mythos_reference: Insider threats, false accusation, security paranoia
episodes.structural_lesson: Secrecy creates incentives to discover a traitor even when the evidence describes a systems failure.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A provenance breach is misread as a Xeno mole, while the actual cause is a Machine archive collision.

episodes.title: Inside Reagan
episodes.mythos_reference: Memory forensics, childhood manipulation, password recovery
episodes.structural_lesson: A memory can be evidence, injury, credential, and editable infrastructure at the same time.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A commander must recover a gate key from a childhood memory without accepting the memory editor’s interpretation of it.

episodes.title: How Reagan Got Her Grove Back
episodes.mythos_reference: Secret-society summit, elite rivalry, informal governance
episodes.structural_lesson: The hidden world is more plausible as overlapping institutions that bargain, compete, and misunderstand one another than as one flawless cabal.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: The Six Hidden Tables convene; each believes the other five are subordinate and none controls the agenda.

episodes.title: Whoas-Feratu
episodes.mythos_reference: Vampiric immortality, celebrity power, blood economy
episodes.structural_lesson: Longevity elites generate succession problems, resource dependencies, and public mythologies around ordinary predation.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: An immortal entertainment syndicate uses legal identity rotation rather than magic to survive, until one member begins harvesting noetic vitality.

episodes.title: Reagan & Mychelle's Hive School Reunion
episodes.mythos_reference: Hive minds, psychoactive origin myths, status performance
episodes.structural_lesson: Collective consciousness still contains embarrassment, hierarchy, memory politics, and competing personal accounts.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A social-memory complex disputes whether an embarrassing founding vision was revelation, intoxication, or both.

episodes.title: We Found Love in a Popeless Place
episodes.mythos_reference: Religious institutions, doctrine management, political theology
episodes.structural_lesson: Controlling an institution is not the same as controlling the transcendent experiences interpreted through it.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: An Archonic identity-spoof operation changes institutional doctrine while leaving the underlying revelation unresolved.

episodes.title: Brettwork
episodes.mythos_reference: Media capture, political puppetry, audience engineering
episodes.structural_lesson: A manufactured leader still depends on audiences, incentives, networks, and the performer’s capacity to deviate.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A Pirate broadcaster becomes the public face of a Human bloc and discovers its audience is a noetic targeting array.

episodes.title: Rontagion
episodes.mythos_reference: Illuminati labor, mind wiping, inter-cabal defection
episodes.structural_lesson: Secret institutions have employees, burnout, ethics disputes, and portability problems when a worker defects.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A memory-erasure specialist seeks asylum carrying techniques that every faction considers both abusive and indispensable.

episodes.title: Project Reboot
episodes.mythos_reference: Mandela effect, alternate histories, reality editing
episodes.structural_lesson: Timeline changes are most legible when treated as branch operations that leave archive conflicts and personal costs.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A Chronology Court discovers that a private family intervention has forked an entire campaign save state.

episodes.title: Appleton
episodes.mythos_reference: Hidden board governance, catastrophe justified as protection, utilitarian population management
episodes.structural_lesson: The most dangerous secret ruler sincerely believes secrecy and engineered crisis are forms of stewardship.
episodes.cosmic_conquest_use: A council offers the player total archive access in exchange for inheriting responsibility for Population Ledger interventions.

design_rules: Use the show to model bureaucracy, incentives, staffing, procurement, inter-agency rivalry, and personal stakes.
Do not treat its premise that conspiracies are true as evidence.
Do not copy characters, organizations, dialogue, episode plots, or visual designs.
Prefer overlapping institutions to one omniscient cabal.
Every impossible system must have an owner, budget, maintenance burden, failure mode, and succession problem.
